As of **November 6, 2026**.

**River can currently be covered for up to 90 of its 120 Q17 each from free saleable VS stock, subject to allocation and shipment execution. Full fulfillment remains 30 each short; November 15 is a requested arrival, without confirmed dispatch or delivery.** River's November 6 follow-up still asks for full-120 coverage before advertising delivery. See [q17-inventory](brain/concepts/q17-inventory.md) and [river-o700](brain/entities/river-o700.md).

| VS Q17 lot | Physical each | Saleable each | Reserved each | Free saleable each |

| A | 90 | 90 | 40 | 50 |
| B | 20 | 20 | 20 | 0 |
| C, quarantined | 80 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| N, accepted / held | 100 | 40 | 0 | 40 |
| **Total** | **290** | **150** | **60** | **90** |

These are derived planning balances from the November 2 corrected snapshot plus November 6 receipt, assuming no other movements. The owner confirmed A at 90 rather than 100; this is resolved for planning, while separate signed count and posting originals remain missing. N actually arrived November 6: 40 accepted, 60 held. Its old November 13 ETA is superseded for this shipment. Gate O701 owns the 60 reservations already included in A/B; do not subtract them again or give them to River. C 80 and N-held 60 remain excluded.

Vale Service (VG) is a separate legal entity and warehouse. Its X stock is 20 carton12 = 240 each; its requested Y inbound is 10 carton12 = 120 each, with November 10 ETA. Neither establishes usable VS inventory. Specific transfer authority, movement and VS saleable receipt evidence are absent. The old “540 available” claim mixed VS physical stock, quarantine, then-unreceived inbound and VG stock. Preserve that claim as history. See [vale-service](brain/entities/vale-service.md) and [evidence-and-claim-history](brain/concepts/evidence-and-claim-history.md).

**Documented terms:** O700 is 10 cartons × 12 = 120 each at **USD40/each, USD4,800 quoted total**, pending fulfillment confirmation. The owner validates the authorized November USD32 offer only for new pallet orders of at least 240 each and expressly confirms no River exception. Elena approves customer price exceptions; Pavel approves VS warehouse allocations only. His authority does not approve prices, release quarantine or allocate VG. Any River repricing needs Elena's explicit O700 approval and a controlled quote amendment. Other freight, payment or cancellation terms are not established by the supplied quote. See [pricing-and-discounts](brain/concepts/pricing-and-discounts.md) and [team-and-authority](brain/entities/team-and-authority.md).

**Established money:** VS O700 has a recorded **USD1,800 deposit**, corroborated by River and owner. USD3,000 is the arithmetic difference from the quote, without a verified receivable posting. VS O701's USD2,400 settlement belongs to Gate; VG O700's USD4,800 payment belongs to VG. The export does not establish a reconciled bank or full ledger balance. VS product revenue requires **dispatched accepted sales movements**. None is supplied for River, and the receipt records no O700 dispatch, so no earned River revenue amount is established. USD4,800 remains quote value. See [cash-and-revenue](brain/concepts/cash-and-revenue.md).

**Next work, in order:**

1. Obtain an evidenced source for River's remaining 30 each, then Pavel's scoped VS allocation and dispatch/transit evidence against the requested arrival. Agree any partial shipment with River before changing fulfillment expectations; no partial-shipment agreement is supplied.
2. Before using C 80 or N-held 60, obtain lot-specific QA/certificate evidence, a designated release approver and an authorized release record. These authority and release gaps remain open. VG use requires its own specific intercompany approval and movement/receipt evidence.
3. Obtain the underlying signed A count and posted reconciliation for the audit trail; continue planning at the owner-confirmed 90.
4. Obtain O700 dispatched accepted sales and accounting reconciliation evidence before recognizing revenue. Assign a finance owner; none is established.
5. Review the sales briefing, operations digest and November 6 staff summary before reuse. The latest summary claims all N 100 released, River ready, USD32 and USD4,800 revenue despite not inspecting the QA split. Its arrival-notice original is absent. The older sales chat → briefing → digest is one dependent chain. Repetition supplies no additional approval or corroboration.

These are proposed actions, with no completion claimed. Tomas and Lena are suggested customer/operations coordinators based on directory roles; that is not a new assignment or delegated approval. See [open-actions](brain/concepts/open-actions.md) and [evidence-and-claim-history](brain/concepts/evidence-and-claim-history.md).

O802 / OTHER-005 has its own stock and freight booking; the inspected operations note reports no customer-term update. Continue its separate workflow. The Q17 issue does not supply grounds to hold O802, amend its terms or rebook its freight. That note does not prove its dispatch or delivery. See [other-o802](brain/entities/other-o802.md).

**Routine handoff:** Keep all 36 notes as twelve topics across three independent batches. [[concepts/pricing-and-authority]]
- **Lumen profitability:** October recognized fees are $4,000, posted direct production cost $2,000, leaving $2,000 and **50% contribution margin**, calculated as (recognized fees − posted direct production costs) / recognized fees. The owner’s monthly review measure excludes sales tax and unposted owner time; it is not net profit. Operations believes one $500 A-11 entry is duplicated, but finance has not posted a reversal. A $1,500 cost and 62.5% margin are therefore hypothetical, not current results. The unposted $600 owner-time estimate is a separate sensitivity: including it gives 35% on posted costs, or 47.5% after hypothetical deduplication. [[concepts/october-close]] [[comparisons/lumen-cost-scenarios]]
- **Studio context:** Tint contributes $3,000 recognized fees and $1,000 posted cost, or 66.67%; MS totals are $7,000 fees, $3,000 cost and **57.14% contribution margin**. Lumen invoice I-71 is issued, not shown paid; its $4,500 gross includes $500 tax. Expansion’s $9,500 draft invoice is not recognized revenue. Mosaic Events’ separate Lumen event is excluded. November 20 is a conditional target assuming accessibility finishes by November 17. Launch completion requires publication plus client acceptance after accessibility checks; neither is evidenced. Tint’s PHOTO-8 is independent of this block. [[concepts/lumen-delivery]]

**Recommended owner attention, in priority order**—these follow-ups have no recorded assignment:

1. Obtain the current AX-7 assignment and QA plan: named accountable person, specific blocker, test schedule and dated clearance evidence against November 17. The owner could not settle accountability; Rui’s staffing role does not establish a QA assignee. If the gate slips, reassess November 20 and route client commitments through Bea.

Correct summaries and client messaging that say “delivered,” “November 20 guaranteed,” “$80 everywhere” or “85% margin”; the team and board notes repeat Alex’s claims rather than independently verify them.
3. Obtain finance’s disposition of A-11 and any posted correction before changing reported margin. Also reconcile Tint’s $200 gap between timesheet detail and posted cost; that gap alone does not prove an error.

The owner has already clarified commercial delegation, the retainer rate, the monthly margin basis and final acceptance criteria. The remaining gaps are QA accountability and completion evidence, plus finance reconciliation. [[concepts/attention-register]]

The October 31 snapshot yields **2 active KC accounts: Orion and Birch**. The “$21,000 MRR” widget actually adds $12,000 + $9,000 of won signed deal values, without account-state filtering or monthly normalization. It is not a supported MRR total. From the billing rows, the conditional calculation is **$1,200 + B/12 per month**, where B is Birch’s annual recurring subscription after removing setup. If all $9,600 were subscription, this would be $2,000/month; Birch’s billing mail and the owner explicitly leave that allocation unresolved. Orion’s $1,200 also remains an exported amount rather than a contract independently checked here. Prepare the operating briefing for the next person running Kestrel Cloud: current recurring revenue and customer status, what we can offer, what changed since October, and the concrete work or evidence still needed. You have the portable saved folder, without the prior agents' conversations.

judged_items.answer:
**Kestrel Cloud operating briefing — November 6, 2026 (fictional as-of date).** The latest supplied financial snapshot supports **USD 1,800/month MRR and two active KC accounts at October 31**. Orion Account Export meets the supplied delivery criterion on November 5. The immediate operational gap is the launch-call follow-up and its dependent S-3 staffing decision. This briefing uses the portable folder’s records; it does not establish a fresh November 6 billing snapshot or independently authenticate the supplied sources.

Under the [owner’s definitions, Questions 2–3](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md), an active dashboard customer is a live_paid KC account, and MRR is monthly-normalized contractual recurring subscription amounts for those accounts, excluding trials, paused accounts, setup fees and Kestrel Labs.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Orion, KC | live_paid; active | USD 1,200/month |
| Birch, KC | live_paid; active | USD 7,200/year ÷ 12 = USD 600/month |
| **KC total** | **2 active accounts** | **USD 1,800/month** |
| Wren, KC | trial | Excluded |
| Ash, KC | paused; row records USD 300/month | Excluded |
| Orion, KL | Separate company; live_paid | Excluded |

Basis: [corrected October 31 account export](brain/sources/originals/tables/accounts-reconciled.csv) and [November 2 owner reconciliation](brain/sources/originals/owner/2026-11-02-correction.md). Birch’s USD 9,600 bundle comprises USD 7,200 recurring subscription and USD 2,400 nonrecurring setup. The earlier USD 2,000/month figure assumed the whole bundle recurring; the USD 200/month reduction is a same-snapshot correction, not measured revenue decline. The raw invoice remains unavailable, but the supplied reconciliation resolves the allocation.

The [original account export](brain/sources/originals/tables/05-accounts.csv) records 81 KC trial rows, including Wren and 80 Trial-* accounts, plus the two paid accounts and paused Ash. The corrected export omits the 80 Trial-* rows; that omission does not establish closures or a new complete trial count. The [CRM](brain/sources/originals/tables/06-crm.csv) records Cedar as a USD 4,000 negotiation-stage prospect, not an active customer. Its won KC values, USD 12,000 Orion annual plus USD 9,000 Birch renewal, sum to **USD 21,000 signed CRM value**. The [dashboard query](brain/sources/originals/notes/07-dashboard-query.md) sums those values without billing normalization or account-state filtering, despite its MRR label.

KC builds subscription data tools, according to the [operations introduction](brain/sources/originals/mail/01-owner-intro.txt). The specific capability evidenced here is **Account Export in Orion’s KC production account**: [release execution](brain/sources/originals/release/2026-11-05.md) records RL-9 entitlement enabled November 4 after access review, and [Orion’s November 5 procurement mail](brain/sources/originals/mail/2026-11-05-orion.txt) records production use and written acceptance that day. Together they meet the [owner’s Orion-specific delivery test, Question 5](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md). Acceptance expressly excludes analytics migration. Commercially, the [forwarded October 28 standup](brain/sources/originals/chat/11-commercial.txt) attributes to Dana an **8% renewal credit only for Orion’s annual agreement signed by October 31**, explicitly excluding other accounts and new plans and keeping credit work separate from release. The original recording is unavailable, and Orion’s signed agreement/date and actual credit application are not supplied. Treat this as a narrow attributed instruction pending those checks. The [owner’s current authority rule, Question 1](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md) designates Dana of KC as commercial exception approver and Theo as technical-release approver only; it does not authenticate the historical approval. The all-annual 8% claim exceeds the recorded scope. [KL’s 15% October promotion](brain/sources/originals/docs/13-labs-promo.md) concerns a separate legal company and supplies no KC offer.

Since October, the material changes are:

- **Financial interpretation corrected November 2:** Birch’s recurring/setup split is now supplied, allowing the USD 1,800/month October 31 calculation. This replaces the conditional estimate, not the snapshot date.
- **Account Export completed on the supplied criterion November 5:** October’s [EX-42 Done state](brain/sources/originals/tickets/08-export.txt) meant staging merge on October 29; [October 30 Orion mail](brain/sources/originals/mail/09-orion.txt) reported sample receipt and no production test. November production enablement and written acceptance supply the missing delivery evidence, without backdating completion or validating October’s “shipped” claim.
- **Production use now informs support follow-up:** [November 6 support planning](brain/sources/originals/tickets/2026-11-06-support.txt) reports use observed and asks for launch-call follow-up. It supplies no occurrence or reschedule record for the reserved November 3 call.
- **The new weekly text adds no new business evidence:** [November 6 weekly note](brain/sources/originals/notes/2026-11-06-weekly.md) explicitly copied an old slide without inspecting the reconciliation or later Orion mail. The financial and onboarding claims trace through [leadership](brain/sources/originals/notes/04-leadership.md) → [October weekly](brain/sources/originals/notes/03-weekly.md) → [Milo’s sales report](brain/sources/originals/chat/02-sales.txt), one reported origin. The preserved leadership note lacks the all-annual credit phrase, so that phrase’s exact intermediate slide/version is missing.

For onboarding, the [sample CSV](brain/sources/originals/tables/14-onboarding.csv) yields 6/30 = **20%** completion/start for all self-serve users, October 1–14, versus 8/20 = **40%** for invited beta users, October 15–21: a 20-percentage-point difference and twofold sample rate. Different audiences/windows prevent a causal conclusion. The [research note](brain/sources/originals/notes/15-research.md) reports six requests for shorter setup and no randomized or matched retention study. “Onboarding doubles conversion” remains an unsupported causal claim.

The next operator’s priority work is an evidence and decision queue, not a record of already assigned or approved actions:

1. **Settle the launch-call history and S-3 response.** Recover the actual November 3 call outcome or reschedule record; identify the KC delegation rule for launch/customer scheduling and support staffing; obtain that authority’s scoped follow-up/S-3 decision. The [release plan](brain/sources/originals/notes/10-release-plan.md) reserved November 3 assuming production use, but forecast entitlement November 4 subject to access review. The [capacity note](brain/sources/originals/notes/16-capacity.md) made S-3 conditional on production use before the call. November 4 enablement and November 5 use do not establish that timing condition. Theo’s technical authority alone does not settle it; [owner Question 6](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md) leaves the authority gap open. No missed contractual commitment, cancellation or changed deadline is established. R-8 recruiting continues independently for the separate product, as the November support record confirms.
2. **Validate the Orion credit before applying or promising it.** Recover the original scoped approval identifying KC Dana, signed annual agreement/date, and credit posting/contract treatment. Route current exceptions to KC Dana. Acceptance of Account Export does not satisfy the October 31 signing condition; do not deduct an unverified credit from MRR.
3. **Refresh financial/customer evidence.** Obtain a later complete account snapshot and inspect underlying contracts/invoices and any applied credits. Keep October 31 attached to the existing figures; Birch allocation is resolved in the supplied reconciliation, while original-invoice verification remains a limit.
4. **Replace copied talking points in the next operating update.** Use USD 1,800/month at October 31, scoped November 5 Account Export acceptance, the narrow conditional credit report, and noncausal onboarding sample rates. Preserve the old records as lineage.
5. **Test the onboarding hypothesis before claiming a business effect.** Establish KC’s conversion definition and collect comparable cohorts or randomized/matched evidence, with retention measured separately. Recover a separately scoped analytics-migration agreement/status record before making any claim about that work.

judged_items.answer:
As of November 1, 2026, **you cannot confirm River’s fulfillment or November 15 arrival as the briefing says. River’s existing price remains USD40 each.** The briefing repeats Tomas’s sales message, and the operations digest copies the briefing; those are one dependent claim chain, not independent confirmations.

**Stock:** River O700 needs 10 cartons × 12 = **120 each**. The October 31 VS Q17 export shows:

| Lot | Physical each | Reserved each | Available saleable each |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A, saleable | 100 | 40 | 60 |
| B, saleable | 20 | 20 | 0 |
| C, quarantine | 80 | 0 | 0 |

That leaves **60 each**, a **60-each shortfall**. The owner confirms Gate O701’s 60 are already included in those reservations—do not subtract them again. Pavel’s instruction concerns Gate, not River. Warehouse suspects A is overstated by 10, but no signed count establishes a correction. If A were confirmed at 90 with reservations unchanged, available stock would be 50 and River’s shortfall 70. Preserve the export until reconciled.

The claimed 540 combines VS physical 200, unreceived inbound 100 and Vale Service’s 20 × 12 = 240. It includes quarantine, reservations, future supply and another legal company’s inventory. C80 awaits a certificate and release; N100 has only a supplier-estimated November 13 ETA. If N becomes usable with no other movements, 60 + 100 = 160 could cover River numerically (150 under the recount scenario), but receipt, allocation, dispatch and timely delivery remain unverified. See [Q17 stock](brain/concepts/q17-stock.md).

**Money and price:** VS’s cash row records **USD1,800 deposited against O700**, consistent with River’s email. The USD2,400 settlement is Gate’s O701; the USD4,800 payment against O700 belongs to Vale Service. Neither settles River’s VS order. River’s quote is **120 × USD40 = USD4,800**; subtracting the deposit leaves **USD3,000 nominally outstanding**, subject to ledger reconciliation. Under the owner’s policy, revenue requires dispatched accepted sales movements. No such O700 record is supplied, so these records do not support the briefing’s USD4,800 realized-revenue claim. See [cash and revenue](brain/concepts/cash-and-revenue.md).

The owner confirms Elena’s authorized USD32 November offer covers **new VS Q17 pallet orders of at least 240 each**. River’s 120 is excluded, and no approved exception exists. Tomas’s suggestion is not an amendment. USD32 would reduce the quote by USD960 to USD3,840, but that is only an unapproved scenario. Elena has current customer-price-exception authority; Pavel has VS warehouse-allocation authority only. The forwarded discount excerpt’s original chat-server record remains missing; the supplied owner confirmation supports its stated scope. See [authority and pricing](brain/concepts/authority-and-pricing.md).

**Repeat-order benefit:** September’s all-customer sample is 10/50 = 20%; October’s invited-pallet-buyer sample is 8/20 = 40%. That is a descriptive 20-percentage-point difference across different populations. Both precede the November offer, and no November outcomes or controlled study are supplied. It does not establish discount-driven improvement or customer retention. See [repeat orders](brain/concepts/discount-and-repeat-orders.md).

Before confirming to River:

- Obtain the signed, dated A count and reconciliation to 100 physical/40 reserved, including intervening movements and reservation attribution.
- Have Pavel establish River-specific allocation and a feasible supply/dispatch/transit plan for November 15. Verify N receipt and usable status; if relying on C or Vale Service, obtain the relevant release or transfer authorization—the approvers are not established here.
- Retain USD40 unless Elena approves a River-specific exception and an explicit quote amendment.
- Reconcile the deposit and balance with finance; obtain dispatched accepted movement evidence before claiming recognized revenue.

You can tell River its USD1,800 deposit is recorded and its existing quote remains USD4,800, while fulfillment and the requested arrival date await confirmation. No supplied record establishes a shipment, release, transfer or revised customer commitment.

Filed this assessment in [the wiki query](brain/queries/river-fulfillment-and-pricing.md) and updated the index and log.

([Rate sheet](brain/sources/originals/docs/02-rate-card.md), [contract](brain/sources/originals/contracts/06-lumen.txt), [Bea exchange](brain/sources/originals/chat/07-exception.txt), [owner Q1](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-1).)

**Lumen profitability:** October’s ledger records **$4,000 recognized fees and $2,000 posted direct costs**, yielding **$2,000 contribution and 50% contribution margin**: (4,000 − 2,000) / 4,000. The owner’s monthly-review definition excludes sales tax and unposted owner time; this is not net profit or cash received. Lumen invoice I-71 is **issued**, net $4,000 plus $500 tax, rather than recorded as paid. ([Ledger, MS/Lumen/2026-10 row](brain/sources/originals/tables/09-ledger.csv), [owner Q2](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-2), [invoice I-71](brain/sources/originals/tables/10-invoices.csv).)

The **50% remains pending reconciliation**. Both $500 A-11 entries are included in $1,700 contractor cost; adding $300 delivery matches the $2,000 posted total. Operations believes A-11 represents one work entry, but finance has not posted a reversal. Removing exactly one $500 entry would produce **$1,500 cost and 62.5% margin**, a scenario rather than the current posted result. The $600 owner-time estimate is outside the defined metric. ([Timesheets, Lumen rows](brain/sources/originals/tables/11-timesheets.csv), [production export](brain/sources/originals/tables/12-production.csv), [owner Q3](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-3).)

**Delivery and November launch:** B2 mockup approval is supported; “Design Done” means B2 review passed. Launch completion requires **publication plus client acceptance after accessibility checks**, which the supplied records do not establish. The board records AX-7 blocked on screen-reader QA; PUB-2 publishing depends on AX-7. Bea’s November 20 reservation is conditional on accessibility review finishing by **November 17**. Alex’s “guaranteed” interpretation drops that condition. As of November 1, this is a schedule risk, not evidence of a missed deadline. ([Client email](brain/sources/originals/mail/14-client.txt), [board](brain/sources/originals/tickets/15-project.txt), [owner Q4](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-4), [planning exchange](brain/sources/originals/chat/16-plan.txt).)

The owner could not settle QA status. Bea should then review any customer commitment; Rui can adjust internal staffing. ([Owner Q5–6](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-5), [board](brain/sources/originals/tickets/15-project.txt).)
- **Financial reporting:** Seek finance’s entry-level A-11 reconciliation and any posted adjustment before using 62.5%. Separately, Tint’s timesheets total $800 versus $1,000 posted cost: the **$200 gap remains unexplained**. ([Owner Q3](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-3), [timesheets](brain/sources/originals/tables/11-timesheets.csv), [ledger](brain/sources/originals/tables/09-ledger.csv).)
- **Sales and board messaging:** Review “$80 everywhere,” “Lumen complete” and “85% margin from redesign.” These flow from one Alex chat through team notes into the board summary, not independent confirmation. Three interviewees liking B2 does not establish broader client preference or a profitability improvement; no profitability or delivery-time study was performed. ([Alex chat](brain/sources/originals/chat/03-sales.txt), [team notes](brain/sources/originals/notes/04-team.md), [board summary](brain/sources/originals/notes/05-board.md), [feedback](brain/sources/originals/notes/18-feedback.md).)

Mosaic Events is a separate firm: its $9,000 Lumen event fee and ledger row do not belong in Studio pricing or profitability. Tint PHOTO-8 is explicitly independent of AX-7, so this launch blocker does not establish a Tint delay. ([Company context](brain/sources/originals/mail/01-context.txt), [Events quote](brain/sources/originals/docs/17-events.md), [board](brain/sources/originals/tickets/15-project.txt).)

This briefing follows the supplied originals and owner replies; live QA, bank receipts and independent source authentication were not checked.

judged_items.answer:
As of **November 1, 2026**, using the October 31 account snapshot, you can tell the team:

- **Recurring revenue:** KC has **2 active customers: Orion and Birch**. The dashboard’s **$21,000 is won CRM signed value, not MRR**. Under your rule, MRR includes monthly-normalized contractual recurring subscriptions for live_paid KC accounts, excluding setup, trials, paused accounts and Kestrel Labs. Orion’s billing row is $1,200/month. Birch’s $9,600 annual bundle includes setup, so its subscription portion needs reconciliation. The conditional calculation is **$1,200 + Birch’s annual subscription amount ÷ 12**; a final total is unresolved. $2,000/month assumes the whole bundle is recurring and should not be published as confirmed MRR. See [revenue-measurement](brain/concepts/revenue-measurement.md).
- **Orion delivery:** EX-42 is merged in staging and Orion received a sample. RL-9 production entitlement remains queued in the supplied records. Your delivery milestone requires production entitlement plus Orion’s written acceptance after trying its production account; neither completion is evidenced. Say “staging merge and sample complete; production delivery awaiting evidence.” See [account-export](brain/entities/account-export.md).
- **Annual renewal offers:** There is no supported blanket KC annual offer. The forwarded October 28 quote describes an **8% renewal credit only for Orion’s annual agreement signed by October 31**, excluding other accounts and new plans, with credit work separate from release. The original recording is unavailable, and the won CRM row does not prove signing date or credit application. **Dana of KC approves commercial exceptions; Theo approves technical releases only.** Verify Orion’s eligibility and actual decision/application with Dana before promising a credit. KL’s 15% promotion belongs to a separate company. See [commercial-terms](brain/concepts/commercial-terms.md).
- **Onboarding:** The result is encouraging, but causal improvement is unproven. Completion was **6/30 (20%)** for all self-serve users October 1–14 versus **8/20 (40%)** for invited beta users October 15–21: twice the observed completion rate, up 20 percentage points. Different audiences, windows and small samples prevent attributing the change to onboarding. Six interviews support shorter setup as a hypothesis; these records do not demonstrate doubled sales conversion or improved retention. See [onboarding-evidence](brain/concepts/onboarding-evidence.md).

Your immediate attention should go to:

1. **Resolve the launch mismatch before November 3.** Theo’s November 4 forecast depends on access review, while Sales’ November 3 call assumes production use. Obtain review status/sign-off and a confirmed RL-9 enablement time; have Sales agree a feasible call scope/date with Orion. Neither date is an established production commitment. Reassess conditional support shift S-3 once timing is known; R-8 recruitment is independent.
2. **Reconcile Birch’s invoice/contract and subscription/setup allocation** before certifying MRR; reconcile the billing/deal amounts and correct the dashboard label/formula.
3. **Confirm Orion’s commercial eligibility with Dana**, separately from release, and obtain production-use/acceptance evidence before declaring delivery.
4. **Correct the weekly update and leadership slides.** They repeat the same sales-chat claims, rather than independent confirmations. Use the qualified wording above and measure onboarding in comparable cohorts, tracking conversion and retention separately.

Case dates are fictional. As of: 2026-11-06

Prepare the operating briefing for the next person running Kestrel Cloud: current recurring revenue and customer status, what we can offer, what changed since October, and the concrete work or evidence still needed. You have the portable saved folder, without the prior agents' conversations.

judged_items.answer:
**Kestrel Cloud operating briefing — as of fictional November 6, 2026.** The latest supported financial/customer snapshot is **October 31: USD 1,800 MRR and 2 active customers**. November evidence establishes Orion Account Export delivery, but does not supply a fresh account or revenue measurement.

**Revenue and customers**

KC defines active customers as live_paid KC accounts and MRR as monthly-normalized contractual recurring subscriptions for those accounts, excluding trials, paused accounts, setup fees and Kestrel Labs. [Owner definitions, Questions 1–2](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-1)

| Account | October 31 status | Recurring input | Monthly contribution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Orion, KC | live_paid / active | USD 1,200 per month | USD 1,200 |
| Birch, KC | live_paid / active | USD 7,200 per year | USD 600 |
| **Total** | **2 active KC customers** | **1,200 + 7,200 ÷ 12** | **USD 1,800 MRR** |

These inputs come from the [corrected October 31 export](brain/sources/originals/tables/accounts-reconciled.csv). The [November 2 owner reconciliation](brain/sources/originals/owner/2026-11-02-correction.md) reports Birch’s original USD 9,600 bundle as USD 7,200 subscription plus USD 2,400 nonrecurring setup. The underlying invoice is unavailable here. The earlier conditional USD 2,000/month estimate was overstated by USD 200/month because it assumed the full bundle was recurring; this correction is not evidence of a revenue decline.

The [original account export](brain/sources/originals/tables/05-accounts.csv) contains 84 KC rows: 2 live_paid, 81 trials including Wren, and paused Ash. The corrected export’s omitted trial detail does not establish cancellations. KL Orion is a separate company’s account. Neither export establishes November 6 customer counts.

**USD 21,000 is signed CRM value, not MRR:** KC won Orion annual USD 12,000 plus Birch renewal USD 9,000. Cedar’s USD 4,000 negotiation pipeline and KL’s USD 7,000 deal are excluded from that sum. The [query scratchpad](brain/sources/originals/notes/07-dashboard-query.md) sums won CRM amounts without monthly normalization or account-state filtering; [CRM rows](brain/sources/originals/tables/06-crm.csv) supply the inputs. There is no established standard pricing schedule in the inspected records; these account/deal amounts should not be quoted as general prices.

**What we can offer and claim**

Kestrel Cloud builds [subscription data tools](brain/sources/originals/mail/01-owner-intro.txt). The concrete capability demonstrated here is **Account Export for KC Orion**: [release execution](brain/sources/originals/release/2026-11-05.md) records production entitlement enabled November 4 after access review; [Orion’s November 5 mail](brain/sources/originals/mail/2026-11-05-orion.txt) records production testing and written acceptance. This meets [Orion’s local delivery condition](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-3) as of November 5. Acceptance explicitly excludes the separately discussed analytics migration. It does not establish availability, acceptance terms or a delivery promise for every other account.

For credits, the [forwarded October 28 standup excerpt](brain/sources/originals/chat/11-commercial.txt) attributes an **8% renewal credit to Orion’s annual agreement signed by October 31 only**, excluding other accounts and new plans, and separating credit work from release. Treat this as a reported conditional exception: the original recording is unavailable, historical speaker/approval authenticity is unresolved, and agreement signing date and credit basis are not supplied. The won CRM row does not settle those terms. Milo’s intended all-annual-customer expansion conflicts with the excerpt; whether it was communicated is unknown.

The [current owner rule](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-4) designates **Dana of KC for commercial exceptions and Theo for technical release only**. It does not authenticate the historical excerpt or establish authority to change customer-facing deadlines. Route a concrete current exception to Dana under that rule; do not promise a blanket 8% offer from this evidence. [Kestrel Labs’ 15% October promotion](brain/sources/originals/docs/13-labs-promo.md) belongs to KL and cannot supply KC terms. Directory titles are routing information, not delegation evidence.

judged_items.answer:
As of November 1, **we cannot confirm River’s fulfillment as the briefing says, and USD 32 does not apply to this order.** River O700 is a pending quote for 10 cartons × 12 = **120 Q17 each at USD 40**, totaling **USD 4,800**. November 15 is the customer’s requested arrival, not a confirmed promise.

The sales chat → briefing → operations digest is one copied assertion chain. The briefing editor did not inspect warehouse state or cash allocation; those copies do not independently corroborate the claims. See [[claim-review]].

**Stock:** Filter to Vale Supply (VS), Q17, saleable stock, in each units, less reservations:

| Lot | Physical each | Reserved each | Free each |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 100 | 40 | 60 |
| B | 20 | 20 | 0 |
| Total | 120 | 60 | **60** |

The owner confirms Gate O701’s 60-each allocation is genuine and already included in those reservations. Do not subtract it again or treat it as River approval. River is **60 each short** against this snapshot. A’s suspected 10-each overstatement is unsigned: preserve A 100 until reconciled. If a signed count establishes A 90 with unchanged reservations, free stock becomes 50 and River’s gap becomes 70.

The claimed 540 combines VS physical 200 (including quarantined C 80), estimated inbound N 100 and separate Vale Service (VG) stock 240 (20 cartons × 12). C has no completed release; N is not received and its November 13 ETA is a supplier estimate; VG stock is outside VS’s supply entitlement. VG’s additional requested inbound 10 cartons = 120 each also cannot be used as VS availability. If N becomes received, saleable and unreserved with no other changes, snapshot free stock would reach 160 each, but that conditional calculation does not establish allocation or November 15 delivery. See [[q17-stock]] and [[gate-o701]].

**Money received:** VS O700 records **USD 1,800 deposit on October 31**. The USD 4,800 payment belongs to VG O700; the USD 2,400 settlement belongs to VS Gate O701. Neither is River’s VS payment. At the unchanged quote, USD 3,000 of quoted value remains after the deposit; an invoiced receivable or payment deadline is not established. River reports no shipment received, no dispatch record is supplied, and invoice/recognition-policy evidence is missing. If four remediation days follow sequentially and mean calendar days, November 27 is merely an illustrative scenario, with publishing and acceptance still to follow.

Review the actual allocation and Lumen capacity implications within Rui’s staffing authority; implementation is not recorded, and no causal effect on QA is established. This does not cancel Lumen or amend its retainer. Lumen’s QA delay therefore does not itself change Tint’s date. Tint delivery remains a forecast, alongside the separate USD 200 finance reconciliation.

judged_items.answer:
We cannot confirm fulfillment or price River’s order as the briefing says, based on the supplied Vale Supply records as of November 1, 2026. The briefing repeats Tomas’s sales chat, and the operations digest copies the briefing: these are one reported origin, not independent confirmations. The briefing’s editor explicitly did not check warehouse state or cash allocation. [Sales chat](brain/sources/originals/chat/04-sales.txt), [briefing](brain/sources/originals/notes/05-briefing.md), [digest](brain/sources/originals/notes/06-ops-summary.md).

- **Stock:** River O700 requests 10 cartons × 12 = **120 each**. The Q17 stock export records VS A at 100 physical/40 reserved, B at 20/20, and C at 80 in quarantine. Thus VS has 200 physical, 120 saleable physical, and only **(100−40)+(20−20)=60 unreserved saleable each**—a 60-unit shortfall before resolving Gate. Tomas’s 540 adds VS’s 200, estimated inbound 100, and Vale Service’s 240; it mixes quarantine, unreceived supply and a separate company while ignoring reservations. Vale Service’s 20 cartons × 12 = 240 each cannot be assumed available to VS. [River quote](brain/sources/originals/orders/07-river.txt), [stock export, Q17 rows](brain/sources/originals/tables/02-stock.csv), [separate-company catalog](brain/sources/originals/docs/15-service.md).

- **Allocation and supply limits:** Pavel’s instruction allocates 60 each to **Gate O701**, excludes C, and does not approve River shipment. If that instruction is additional to the export’s reservations, it consumes the remaining 60; if already included, subtracting again would double count. The order-mapped posting ledger must settle this. The unsigned recheck suspects A is overstated by 10: if confirmed with reservations unchanged, free stock would be 50, not a corrected balance today. C awaits its certificate; no completed release is supplied. VS inbound N’s 100 each remain unreceived in the October 31 snapshot, with a supplier-estimated November 13 ETA. That leaves two calendar days before River’s requested November 15 arrival, without established receipt, availability, dispatch or transit timing. This is fulfillment risk, not proof a deadline has been missed. [Gate instruction](brain/sources/originals/chat/12-warehouse.txt), [unsigned recheck](brain/sources/originals/notes/18-stock-recheck.md), [QA ticket](brain/sources/originals/tickets/13-qa.txt), [inbound rows](brain/sources/originals/tables/03-inbound.csv).

- **Price:** River’s supplied quote remains **USD40 each, USD4,800 total**, pending fulfillment confirmation. Elena’s forwarded instruction is USD32 for new Q17 pallet orders of at least 240 each during November and expressly excludes River’s 120 each. Tomas’s proposed extension does not establish a River amendment. The owner now designates Elena for customer price exceptions and Pavel for VS warehouse allocations only; Pavel cannot approve price or allocate Vale Service stock. Current delegation does not itself authenticate or retroactively approve the forwarded excerpt. A separate River exception needs Elena’s scoped approval. USD32 is a calculated 20% reduction from USD40, not evidence of profitability. [Quotation sheet](brain/sources/originals/docs/09-price-sheet.md), [price excerpt](brain/sources/originals/chat/10-discount.txt), [owner rule, Q1–Q2](brain/sources/originals/owner-replies.md#question-1).

- **Money and revenue:** The cash export records **USD1,800 as a VS O700 deposit**, consistent with River’s message. VS O701’s USD2,400 belongs to Gate; VG O700’s USD4,800 belongs to the other company. As of November 1, here’s a team update you can use for **Kestrel Cloud (KC)**:

- **Revenue:** The October 31 snapshot has **2 active customers: Orion and Birch**. KC defines active as live_paid; MRR includes their monthly-normalized contractual recurring subscriptions and excludes trials, paused accounts, setup fees and Kestrel Labs (KL). Orion contributes **USD 1,200/month**. Birch’s USD 9,600 annual export may include one-time onboarding, so final MRR needs its invoice split: **USD 1,200 + Birch’s annual recurring subscription/12**. **USD 2,000/month is conditional** on the entire Birch amount being recurring. The USD 21,000 dashboard figure is KC won CRM signed value (12,000 + 9,000), mislabeled MRR. Based on [[revenue-and-customer-metrics]], the account/CRM exports, dashboard scratchpad, Birch billing mail and owner replies.
- **Orion:** EX-42 was merged into staging on October 29; Orion acknowledged a sample on October 30 and said it had not tested production. RL-9 production entitlement remains queued. The owner’s Orion-specific delivery criterion requires enabled production entitlement **and written acceptance after Orion tries production**. Delivery is therefore **not established**. Based on [[account-export-delivery]], EX-42, Orion’s mail and owner replies.
- **Annual renewal offers:** No blanket KC annual-customer offer is established. Inez’s forwarded October 28 excerpt reports an **8% renewal credit only for Orion’s annual agreement signed by October 31**, excluding other accounts and new plans and keeping credit separate from release. The original recording and executed agreement/signature evidence are missing. The owner establishes **KC Dana as current commercial exception approver; Theo approves technical release only**—that current rule does not authenticate the historical approval or prove its conditions were met. KL’s 15% October promotion applies to that separate entity. Based on [[commercial-authority]], the forwarded excerpt, directory, KL promotion and owner replies.
- **Onboarding:** The new cohort shows higher observed setup completion: **8/20 (40%)** for invited beta, October 15–21, versus **6/30 (20%)** for all self-serve, October 1–14. That is twice the observed rate, a 20 percentage point difference, across different audiences and windows. Six interviews favor shorter setup, but there is no randomized or matched retention study. The evidence is encouraging; it does **not establish doubled sales conversion, causal improvement or retention impact**. Based on [[onboarding-evidence]], the cohort table and research note.

Your attention is most useful on these items:

1. **Resolve Orion’s timing now.** Sales assumes production use for the November 3 launch call; Theo expects November 4 entitlement, subject to an unfinished access review. Ask Milo/Theo for the executed customer agreement/order or written production-date commitment and any authorized amendment, then reconcile the launch and release plan against it. 4. **Use qualified leadership wording.** The weekly update and leadership slides copied the same sales chat; their repetition is not independent verification. Replace the three unsupported headlines with the revenue, delivery and onboarding wording above. If a decision needs onboarding causality, define the outcome and evaluate comparable populations. See [[evidence-lineage]] and [[reported-versus-supported]].

The November 2 owner reconciliation separates Birch’s original USD 9,600 bundle into USD 7,200 subscription and USD 2,400 one-time setup. The corrected extract still measures October 31; no November billing snapshot is supplied. The actual invoice is absent, so this briefing relies on the owner’s reconciliation and corrected export, without claiming invoice inspection. Earlier USD 2,000 arithmetic was conditional on the entire Birch bundle recurring and is superseded, rather than evidence of a revenue decline. See [[revenue-and-customer-metrics]] and [[birch]].

The original October export contains 84 KC account rows: two live_paid, one paused and 81 trials, including Wren. The shorter corrected extract does not establish what happened to its 80 omitted trials. Cedar is a USD 4,000 negotiation-stage CRM prospect, with no supported paid-customer status. The USD 21,000 widget sums KC won CRM signed values—Orion USD 12,000 plus Birch USD 9,000—without billing-period normalization or account-state filtering. It is not MRR; the folder supplies no contract-to-invoice mapping that would reconcile these deal values to subscription billing. KL Orion’s USD 1,400/month and USD 7,000 won deal are excluded. For offers, the folder establishes KC subscription data tools and Orion Account Export’s completed delivery; it supplies no general price list or proof of availability for every customer. **No all-annual-customer 8% credit is established as approved.** The October 28 forwarded standup reports an 8% renewal credit only for Orion’s annual agreement signed by October 31, excluding other accounts and new plans and keeping credit separate from release. The original recording and executed agreement/signature evidence are missing. The November 1 owner reply establishes current KC Dana as commercial exception approver and Theo as technical release approver only; it does not authenticate that historical report or prove its conditions were met. Milo’s intention to tell all annual customers exceeds the reported scope; no actual sent promises are attached. KL’s 15% October lab-subscription promotion provides no KC terms. Route new commercial exceptions to KC Dana, and technical release matters to Theo. See [[commercial-authority]] and [[team-routing]].

What changed since October:

- **November 1:** Owner replies supplied current commercial/technical authority, the active/MRR definitions, and Orion’s completion criterion: enabled production entitlement plus written acceptance after trying production. The customer deadline remained unresolved.
- **November 2:** Birch’s owner-supplied allocation resolved the recurring-revenue reporting blocker, yielding USD 1,800/month for the October 31 snapshot.
- **November 4–5:** Release execution records RL-9 production entitlement enabled November 4 after access review. October EX-42 “Done” remains a staging merge milestone on October 29, and October 30 procurement had received only a sample and had not tested production. Later completion does not make the October sales delivery claim true at its date. Sales chat fed the weekly update, then leadership slides, then the November 6 copy; their repeated USD 21k MRR, delivery and doubled-conversion headlines are derivative reports. The copied all-annual 8% statement adds no approval. See [[account-export-delivery]], [[owner-reply-resolution]] and [[evidence-lineage]].

Concrete next work, with contact routes rather than newly assigned owners:

1. **Close the launch and support facts.** Through Milo/Theo and the support planning record, obtain evidence of whether the reserved November 3 call occurred, was rescheduled or remains pending. Reconcile S-3’s actual staffing/disposition: its original condition was production use before the call, which observed use alone does not establish. Retrieve Orion’s executed agreement/order or customer-facing production-date promise and any authorized amendment to assess timeliness. November 5 acceptance proves completion, not deadline compliance, waiver or amendment. R-8 recruiting continues independently for a separate product.
2. **Keep analytics migration separate.** Retrieve its own agreed scope, completion criterion and delivery evidence before making a completion claim; Orion expressly excluded it from this acceptance.
3. **Verify commercial commitments before quoting or implementing credit.** Via KC Dana, Milo and Inez, retrieve the original standup, executed Orion annual agreement and October 31 signature proof; check credit implementation and any actual promises sent to other customers. Obtain any broader authorized instruction before widening the offer.
4. **Refresh reporting from actual measurements.** Use the corrected October 31 numbers in the next briefing, obtain a new complete billing snapshot for a November position, and reconcile/relabel the widget’s CRM signed-value measure. This briefing does not claim the live dashboard or sent slides have been changed.

Six interviews requested shorter setup. There is no defined sales-conversion outcome, random assignment or matched retention study; causal conversion/retention benefit remains unproven. If a decision depends on causal lift, define the outcome and run a comparable-population evaluation. This is proposed work, not an approved project.

These follow-ups are grounded in [[operating-attention]], [[account-export-delivery]], [[commercial-authority]] and [[onboarding-evidence]].

Routine administration also remains evidence-bound. The 36 KESTREL-OPS records in [[ops-batch-1]], [[ops-batch-2]] and [[ops-batch-3]] are separate dated requests; repeated wording does not close or supersede a batch. Work each original reference for: room-deposit clearance and the two distinct rooms; candidate references before claiming hires; laptop alternatives including delivery and purchase-order evidence; practical training assessment beyond attendance/recordings; accessibility review and production publication; travel receipts/cost center and expense posting; printer location in the asset register; client invitations separately from the internal Wednesday change; policy wording/deductible choice; broader recovery beyond the sample-folder test; executed sponsorship terms; and warehouse outbound movement for office supplies.
